angle: WR/TE break mechanics: one metric (Break G: average g over the second around the first cut, covering braking in, turning and driving out), graded by the same code on Combine route drills and on sampled NFL snaps of the same route family (slant/out/hitch/in/corner). Tested against full-season NGS separation over expected on held-out draft classes. New this round: a same-snap Sunday check with a timing placebo.
metric_name: Break G (how hard a receiver plants: average g over the one second around his first real cut; z-scored within drill and Combine year, averaged over drills, shrunk by between-drill reliability)
headline_number: -1.2 in of career SOE per sd of drill Break G [90%: -3.7, +1.0], n=116, held out by draft class vs the pre-set no-tracking forecast. Ridge-shrunk forecast -0.9 [-3.2, +1.4]. A within-class shuffle placebo gives 90% of slopes in [-2.2, +2.2], and 38% are as extreme as the real one. Drill-to-NFL Break G rho -0.05 (n=101) vs official 40 to NFL top speed 0.46 (n=100). A top-third rule flags about 17 receivers a class, drafted about 20 slots early, for +0.9 in SOE [-2.1, +3.8].
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round 23 cand_2 (8.24), applying the judges' general top_changes. (1) Placebo: Break G shuffled within class, 2000 times (Fig 3B), replacing the simulation panel, which moved to the appendix. (2) A ridge-shrunk baseline (penalty chosen inside the training classes) added to the three earlier ones; held-out R2 for all four in Table 1. (3) New Section 3 and Fig 4: same-man, same-snap test of NFL Break G vs separation at the throw, within receiver x route family, controlling for cushion and cut-to-throw time. It shows +6.2 in/sd on all snaps but +1.1 [-8.1, +10.2] on random snaps, and the post-throw timing placebo reads -13.5, so the Sunday link is play context. This reconciles the halves: NFL Break G vs career SOE is -0.15 (n=101). (4) Monday action is a fixed top-third rule with the expected 2026 count (about 17), the draft cost (about 20 slots at median pick 133) and its separation return. (5) Table 2 adds a tracking-located clip (season, week, quarter, clock, route, g, yards open) per named receiver for film confirmation, stated as not yet watched. (6) Viz: Fig 1 uses direct labels instead of a legend; Fig 2B has fixed-column n labels and an added NFL Break G to SOE row; Fig 4 (cards) has unclipped intervals, a within-class rank on every label and averages in the title; n is in every caption. (7) Plain-language pass (no LOCO/Spearman jargon), a why-now paragraph, lede numbers stated once, and the reliability/power simulation moved to the appendix. 1,978 words, 5 figures + 2 tables.
open_risks: Still a null-result paper; the re-stem prescription and the top-third strike rule are untested proposals.
Clips in Table 2 are located by tracking only; nobody has watched them, so 'film-verified' is not met.

Section 3 is descriptive: with no defenders or ball, the same-snap link cannot be separated from play context, and the before/after-throw split was chosen after a first look at the data (an uncontrolled first look gave +6.3, +6.0 and +3.9 in/sd for cut-offs of 0, 0.2 and 0.3 s before the throw; those figures are not in numbers.json).
Braking transfer (+0.12) is one of 30 grid cells with no multiplicity correction.
Top-third SOE difference (+0.9) is raw, while the main slope (-1.2) is adjusted for the forecast, so the signs differ; both intervals span zero.
Not blind: all three classes were seen in earlier rounds; the ridge row, placebo and Section 3 were added after the main test was frozen.
Game tracking is a 40-play sample, half top-EPA, with no defenders or ball; analysis.py takes about 75 s.
